about: Illustrative assumptions for cargorm.html. Not any airline's data.

aircraft.name: Widebody belly
aircraft.blurb: The lower deck of a long-haul passenger widebody: about 16 t and 110 m³ left for cargo once bags, fuel and passengers are loaded.

aircraft.name: Main-deck freighter
aircraft.blurb: A large twin-engine freighter on a long sector: about 95 t and 580 m³ of usable space after pallet contours and packing losses.

demand.name: Balanced
demand.blurb: General cargo, some e-commerce and a little pharma, at about the IATA volume ratio on average.

demand.name: E-commerce peak
demand.blurb: Light, bulky parcels: the hold cubes out long before it weighs out.

demand.name: Heavy industrial
demand.blurb: Machinery, parts and other dense freight: weight runs out first.

variability.name: Low
variability.blurb: Half the base no-show rates; tendered weight 85–105% of booked.

variability.name: Medium
variability.blurb: Base no-show rates; tendered weight 70–110% of booked.

variability.name: High
variability.blurb: 1.6 times the base no-show rates; tendered weight 55–115% of booked.
